threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a 'bus stop' instead of a 'bus shelter' like everyone else around here. The locals know, it’s the little things that matter.
Caught a night bus from Brixton to Clapham last weekend; the driver serenaded us with classic Motown all the way. Best ride of the night!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Last Sunday, I saw a guy in a pink suit juggling flaming torches while his dog waited patiently for a hot dog. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Döner spot that serves vegan kebabs at 3 AM, buzzing with late-night debates about art and politics.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their nonchalance when BART's a mess; tourists freak out while we just roll our eyes and grab a burrito.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 38 Geary at 5 PM—door wouldn’t close, driver just shrugged. We sat for 10 mins while tourists took selfies in the chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all trendy bars, but on any given morning, our quiet plazas echo with locals’ morning chats over cafés, not cocktails.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their confusion at the multi-stop, forever-spiraling route of the 24 bus - they think it's a shortcut.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the Clissold Park café is a secret gem, not just the usual Saturday brunch spot packed with strollers.
Last night on the 196, a guy sang 'Wonderwall' karaoke-style, and a group of kids joined in. Bus driver just rolled his eyes and kept driving.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a wild rabbit munching on a discarded döner kebab under the U-Bahn station. Only in Neukölln, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you stumble upon a kebab shop that opens at 3 AM and serves vegan döner alongside your late-night currywurst fix.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they know the shortcut past the construction on Valencia; tourists just wait in line at the detour.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading the bus passengers at Civic Center, full-on opera. Muni folks didn’t miss a beat—clapped as the bus pulled away.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but the real treasures are the hidden plazas where locals sip vermut and chat, away from the crowds.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by the way they still use Google Maps to navigate the short streets of Gràcia, looking up at the buildings like they're on a treasure hunt.
